raw_response:
I am still doing what I know best: keep the main land in wheat-maize, and leave a small piece for cotton. At my age I do not like making big changes unless I see a very strong reason. Wheat-maize is still the steady way here in Quzhou. It keeps grain coming and spreads the risk. Cotton can still bring cash, but it takes more watching and more picking, so I will not put too much area into it.

I finished middle school, so I do pay some attention to what the extension people say, but I still farm mostly by what I have seen on my own fields and what the neighbors do. If I push fertilizer too low, I worry the crop will look weak and yield will fall. But fertilizer, pumping water, and labor all cost money, and some people in my family work off-farm, so I cannot manage everything too intensively. This year I will stay with a moderate plan: wheat gets enough base fertilizer and one topdress, maize goes in right after wheat harvest with simple field prep, and cotton stays on a small area where I can manage it carefully.
